tier_reason: LEADERBOARD.md's 'Speed and cost by hardware' table shows Tesseract 5 vs EasyOCR pages/s exactly as claimed (3.47 vs 1.11 G4, 0.81 vs 0.49 A100-40GB, 0.82 vs 0.45 L4, 0.68 vs 0.34 T4, 2.28 vs 0.20 TPU-v6e-1). Harness code (ocrbench/engines/tesseract.py, easyocr_engine.py, worker.py) and CPU models (per-run env.json) are public, but Tesseract is an apt package (5.3.4 per status.json) with no compiler or flags stated, and the harness is a 0-star single-author repo rather than a well-known suite, so C, not A or B.

corrections.hardware: Google Colab runtimes, CPU models from each run's env.json: G4 = NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition with AMD EPYC 9B45, 48 vCPU, 176.9 GB RAM; A100-40GB with Intel Xeon CPU @ 2.20GHz, 12 vCPU; L4 with Intel Xeon CPU @ 2.20GHz, 12 vCPU; T4 with Intel Xeon CPU @ 2.00GHz, 8 vCPU; TPU-v6e-1 VM host AMD EPYC 9B14, 44 vCPU (classic engines run on the host CPU).
corrections.workload: OCR throughput in pages per second (total pages divided by summed batch-pass wall time) over the standard profile (215 pages: 50 historical book pages, 50 olmOCR-bench document pages, 60 IAM handwriting lines, 5 synthetic stress pages at 11 degradation levels = 55) on five Colab runtime types. Tesseract 5.3.4 (distro package via pytesseract, LSTM --oem 1 --psm 3, eng+fra+deu+lat) runs one process per page across all vCPUs with OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=1; EasyOCR 1.7.2 (torch 2.11.0+cu130, CRAFT+CRNN, readtext batch_size=16) runs one page at a time in a single process, on the GPU on GPU runtimes and on the host CPU on the TPU VM.
corrections.caveats: Third-party, single-author harness (kvenanzi/ocr, 0 stars, 48 commits, no repository license shown, earliest runs dated 2026-10-02), not peer reviewed and not a well-known suite. The speed rows are not like-for-like: Tesseract OCRs pages in parallel across every vCPU (48 workers on G4, 44 on the TPU host, 12 on A100/L4, 8 on T4) while EasyOCR processes pages one at a time on one GPU, so the win comes from page-level process parallelism. On single-page latency (p50 from leaderboard hardware.csv) GPU EasyOCR is faster on three of four GPU runtimes: G4 0.90 s vs 1.38 s, A100 2.07 s vs 2.92 s, L4 2.27 s vs 2.92 s; Tesseract wins only on T4 (2.69 s vs 3.31 s) and the TPU host CPU (1.89 s vs 5.92 s). On G4 the per-track throughput win is concentrated in books (7.39 vs 0.69 pages/s) and docs (5.27 vs 0.66); on the degraded stress track EasyOCR is slightly faster (1.264 vs 1.224 pages/s). The TPU-host Tesseract and EasyOCR rows come from two different runs (20261004-205730 and 20261005-140416, same EPYC 9B14 host type). Tesseract tested is the distro 5.3.4 build, not current main; build flags and compiler are not stated, so this is not tier A. Standard profile is about 215 pages and the README notes small samples. Tesseract loses throughput to PaddleOCR 3 (4.13 vs 3.47 pages/s on G4, and also on T4, L4 and A100), PaddleOCR-VL 1.6 (5.84 on G4) and OvisOCR2 (3.66 on G4), and to docTR on A100 (1.03 vs 0.81). Accuracy context from the same page: Tesseract 67.8% overall vs EasyOCR 60.4%, but 56.1% CER on handwriting. The project's own tessdoc Benchmarks.md (https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tessdoc/blob/main/Benchmarks.md) only compares Tesseract versions and build flags on one image on Windows 10, VS 2019, i7-10750H (e.g. tessdata_best: 4.1.3 without AVX 37.6052 s, with AVX 12.7300 s, 5.0.1 6.1981 s, 5.0.1 OpenMP 3.4590 s), and shows 3.05 with the legacy engine faster than 5.0.1 on the plain tessdata model (2.4713 s vs 2.9107 s), so it gives no external-baseline win. EasyOCR is not a recognized incumbent for Tesseract (Tesseract is itself the incumbent classic OCR engine). Category image-codecs is the closest wave-10 category; OCR is image analysis, not a codec.

notes: Numbers match the leaderboard exactly and the derived ratios (3.1x G4, 1.65x A100, 1.8x L4, 2.0x T4, 11.4x TPU host) are correct, so tier C stands. Main shortcomings to record: unequal parallelism (Tesseract multi-process across all vCPUs vs EasyOCR one page at a time on one GPU; EasyOCR has lower single-page latency on G4, A100 and L4), unknown 0-star harness, distro Tesseract 5.3.4 with unstated build flags, slower than PaddleOCR 3 and PaddleOCR-VL, and wrong category (OCR, not a codec). Metadata checked on github.com: Apache-2.0, 76.9k stars, not archived or a fork, last commit 2026-10-10.
